findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's credentials would allow complete control over compute, storage, serverless, and monitoring in the account, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via EC2/Lambda role passing.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the service user and its secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no pgp_key is supplied, so encrypted_secret will be empty and secret/ses_smtp_password are written to state unencrypted). Long-lived static keys attached to a highly privileged user create a durable credential theft target with no automatic rotation.

A long-lived IAM user is used for service/deployment access with broad permissions and no MFA condition or boundary policy, instead of an assumable role with temporary credentials. force_destroy = true also allows silent removal of attached keys and policies masking credential changes.

The access key material is exposed as a Terraform output without sensitive = true, so it is printed to the console and CI logs and stored in state; since no pgp_key was set on the access key, this output path surfaces credential material to anyone with log or state access.
